title: CILantro blocker report
description: `cilantro/NAME.blockers.json`: what stopped a run, and what to declare to get past it. This is the file a caller reads between one run and the next.

DeclarationsName.description: What the declarations file called itself, so a decision can be shown to have been made about this one.

CallsAllowed.description: Whether the run was given --allow-declared-calls, without which anything declared about a call is ignored.

Blockers.description: What stopped the run, in the order first hit.

UnconsultedDeclarations.description: What was declared and never asked about. Usually a key spelled differently from the one the run asks under, which is a different mistake from a declaration that did not work.

ContinuedPast.description: What the run met and carried on past, which a strict run would have stopped at. Worth reading when the result looks wrong, and not otherwise.

blocker.title: One thing that stopped a run

Kind.description: Which sort of stop this is, which is to say what would get past it.

Key.description: What the stop is about — a fact key, a method signature, a native entry point, a budget name — which is also what makes two occurrences the same occurrence.

Remedy.description: What to write in a declarations file to get past this. Null where no declaration will, and the next step is a change to the tool.

Declare.description: The same remedy written out as a line of the file, for a person. Derived from Remedy; a program should use Remedy.

remedy.title: A declaration that would get past a stop
remedy.description: Applying one is `declarations[Section][Name] = Value` and nothing else. Where Wants is null the value is complete and can be applied without a decision; where it is not, Value holds exactly one null standing where the caller's answer goes.

Section.description: Which part of the declarations file this goes in.

Name.description: The key within that section, spelled as the run asks for it.

Value.description: What to write there. A budget carries a figure already, as a starting point rather than a promise: a step budget starts at 10000000 and doubles from there, and every other budget is twice what was refused.

Wants.description: What the caller has to decide, named as a type where the tool knows one. Null where the tool filled the value in itself.

Flag.description: A switch the run needs as well as the declaration.
